s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly growing eyelid mass with recent changes and crust formation
salient_findings: Yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule on the central lower eyelid
Flakier surface at one lateral end
Hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts and neoplastic squamous cell proliferation
key_facts: 4-year history of a left lower eyelid mass
Recent growth and crust formation
Papule is well-circumscribed and located on the central lower eyelid
Tumor has a flakier surface at one lateral end
Specimen measured 0.8 × 0.5 × 0.3 cm
Hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells
Malignant squamous cells have eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli
Mitotic figures are present
Central areas of clear cell change are periodic acid-Schiff positive and diastase sensitive

raw.rationale: The presence of a hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts, proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells, and a well-circumscribed papule with a flakier surface at one lateral end are characteristic features of verrucous carcinoma.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While squamous cell carcinoma can present with similar features, the well-circumscribed nature and hyperkeratotic appearance of the lesion are more suggestive of verrucous carcinoma.

rejected.label: Keratoacanthoma
rejected.why: Keratoacanthoma typically has a more rapid growth phase and often resolves on its own, which is not consistent with the 4-year history of the lesion in this case.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ with invasive components
rejected.why: The presence of malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli suggests invasive disease, but the overall appearance is more consistent with verrucous carcinoma.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma with clear cell features
rejected.why: While the lesion does have clear cell features, the overall clinical and histopathological appearance is more suggestive of verrucous carcinoma.

gold: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma arising in a seborrheic keratosis of the eyelid
